clue.text: Excitement as tension explodes

indicators.note: something that explodes flies apart, so the letters of the two words are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nervous strain builds until it bursts out as excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explodes' signals the anagram of AS plus TENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a stir of thrilled public interest, a synonym for excitement.

clue.text: Working steam-mill of no great importance

indicators.note: working letters are being worked into a new shape, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A small steam-powered mill in operation is not very significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' signals the anagram of STEAMMILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time describes something minor or insignificant in scale.

clue.text: She tends to rush over certain points

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for rush is read backwards

parts.note: to run is to rush
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A carer hurries across certain spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She tends to' reads as 'she usually'; 'tends' is the definition, a carer. 'over' turns RUN into NUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is a woman who looks after the sick, the classic carer.

clue.text: "Hell is full of musical -:music is the brandy of the damned" (Shaw)

definitions.text: "Hell is full of musical -:music is the brandy of the damned" (Shaw)

parts.words: "Hell is full of musical -:music is the brandy of the damned" (Shaw)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shaw's Man and Superman, mocking unskilled music-makers

explanation.surface: A quotation from Bernard Shaw about bad musicians in Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's line says Hell teems with untrained music-makers, people who play for love rather than as professionals.

clue.text: Thought the holy man about 51 a visionary

parts.note: an idea is a thought

indicators.note: about here means close by, so the holy man is set next to the number

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
ST is the abbreviation for a saint

explanation.surface: A holy man of about fifty-one is thought to be a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 51' reads as an age; LI is Roman 51, with ST placed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty ideals, a dreamer who sees how things could be.

clue.text: A head with totally unsatisfactory delivery

parts.note: nob is slang for a head
all means totally, completely

explanation.surface: A head teacher gives a dreadful speech.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a no-ball is an illegal delivery by the bowler, which does not count and gives the batting side a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-ball is a bowled ball that breaks the rules, an unacceptable throw to the batsman.

clue.text: Being amusing, it dispels gloom

definitions.meaning: ... entertainment or ... verse is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: Humour that lifts a dark mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means entertaining and not serious, and it is also the brightness that drives away darkness.

clue.text: God against Russell's view of ghosts

parts.note: a Lar is a Roman household god
V is short for versus, against
AE was the pen name of the Irish poet George William Russell

explanation.surface: A deity is set against a philosopher's opinion on the supernatural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russell' suggests the philosopher Bertrand; it is the Irish poet George Russell, who signed himself AE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman belief larvae were malevolent spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Trial -. a dog's involved, a fighter

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A dog features in a court case about a combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' signals the anagram of TRIAL, A and DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman who fought in the arena for public entertainment.

clue.text: Some actresses do their own hair

indicators.note: some of the word, a run of letters inside it, gives the answer

explanation.surface: Not every actress pays a hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks a run of letters from 'actresses'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: About to cut a prison stretch

indicators.note: one word is said to cut into another, so the short word goes inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of slicing time off a jail sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' looks like prison slang for a sentence, which the surface plays on; it is the definition, an expanse of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area of land, a stretch of ground measured in acres.

clue.text: Check, blow up, and fire a lot

parts.note: to bar is to check or stop
to rage is to blow up in anger

explanation.surface: A list of commands to an artillery crew: halt, explode, then shoot heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, sustained bombardment by guns.

clue.text: A Belgian university subject

definitions.meaning: a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse, home to a well-known university
a vassal, a feudal subject owing loyalty to a lord

explanation.surface: Someone names an academic topic studied in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' reads as a field of study but is the feudal sense: a vassal.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a Belgian city with its own university, and in feudal law a liege is a vassal bound to serve a lord.

clue.text: Given tranquillisers, a bull in a frenzy lies captured

indicators.note: the word lies holds the scrambled letters prisoner inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a frenzied bull charges wildly, so its letters with a are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A raging bull is sedated and then lies there, caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' looks like part of a dose; it only links. A BULL scrambled gives ULLAB, held inside LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lullabies are soothing songs that calm a child to sleep, playfully called tranquillisers.

clue.text: The diversion of profits

definitions.meaning: a pastime or hobby that holds the attention
the money earned on a loan or deposit

explanation.surface: Someone describes the diverting of company earnings elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' suggests money being redirected, but it means a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a hobby or pastime, and interest is also the return earned on capital.

clue.text: Convey delight

definitions.meaning: to carry from one place to another

explanation.surface: Pass on joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport goods is to carry them, and a transport of joy is a rapture.

clue.text: A highlight of the night that's clear

definitions.text: A highlight of the night that's clear

parts.words: A highlight of the night that's clear
parts.note: a point of light that shines in a cloudless night sky, with a hint at the leading performer of an evening show

explanation.surface: The best moment of an evening out, plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars are the bright points seen in a cloudless sky after dark, and a star is also the highlight of a show.

clue.text: Substitute for military personnel now

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the present is now

explanation.surface: Replacement soldiers are wanted at once.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to act in their stead, standing in on their behalf.

clue.text: Refuse to put a philosopher in jug? Quite the reverse!

indicators.note: one word is put in another to make a container
this flips the order the clue states: the philosopher goes round the jug, not into it

parts.note: a sage is a wise man, a philosopher
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: Someone declines to lock up a thinker, preferring to lock the jug in him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, waste. 'in' alone would put the philosopher inside the jug; 'Quite the reverse' swaps that.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is the waste matter carried off by drains, refuse in another word.

clue.text: The outlook for a class of people going about quietly

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the word for a group goes round the quiet letter

parts.note: a sect is a class or group of people
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A forecast for some group moving around silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' puts P (piano, quietly) inside SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a view or an expectation of what lies ahead.

clue.text: Romance found in retirement in Israel

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for a romance is read backwards

parts.note: a romance is a story, a tale

explanation.surface: A love affair blossoms after someone retires to Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses TALE. Elat (also Eilat) is Israel's Red Sea port, so the definition is a place found in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elat is a port town at the southern tip of the country, on the Gulf of Aqaba.

clue.text: A sign of distress brings rent reduction

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
a drop is a fall or reduction

explanation.surface: A tenant is upset, or relieved, by a cut in what they pay the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' reads as the payment for housing; here it is a rip, the past of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset sheds tears, so a single falling bead from the eye shows sorrow.

clue.text: A moving proposal

parts.note: reads as a touching marriage offer, but means a formal suggestion that someone moves at a meeting, as well as movement itself

explanation.surface: A heartfelt offer of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal proposal put before a meeting is said to be moved, and movement is also motion.

clue.text: Clever bishop, on the conservative side

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for a bishop
the right is the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: A smart bishop leans towards the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent and quick-witted.

clue.text: Talk the underworld way

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a course is a way or route

explanation.surface: A guide to how people speak in criminal circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests gangsters, but it is the classical realm of the dead, ruled by Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal conversation or a spoken or written treatment of a topic.

clue.text: Bearing in some animals, administers medication

indicators.note: the bearing is placed in the word for animals

parts.note: does are female deer or rabbits
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A vet treats some animals while they are giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' suggests carrying young; it is a compass direction, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses is a verb meaning gives measured amounts of a medicine.

clue.text: Humble woman embracing a Mohammedan leader

indicators.note: the word for a woman holds the other letters in its arms

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A modest woman hugs a Muslim chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' looks like an adjective describing the woman but is a verb. 'embracing' puts A and M ('Mohammedan leader') inside SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to humiliate them, to put them to disgrace.

clue.text: A sound opener to admire

indicators.note: sound here means spoken, so the word for an opener is said aloud

parts.note: a door is an opener, a way in, and said aloud it gives the ending heard in the answer

explanation.surface: A reliable start to praising someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' reads as 'reliable'; it signals that the phrase A DOOR is said aloud, the A kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to admire and love them deeply.

clue.text: Pole, having to fly, packing

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
taken as written
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: A Polish traveller gets ready for a flight by putting things in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is a geographical pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowing means packing things neatly away in a place.

clue.text: A people backing one could be a bloomer

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for people is read in reverse

parts.note: men are people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd supporting one candidate might make a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder; here it is something that blooms, a flower. 'backing' turns MEN into NEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a garden flower, so it is one example of a plant that blooms.

clue.text: It's an odd sort of stuff

indicators.note: an odd sort of version is a strange rearrangement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs at a strange material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd sort of' rearranges the letters of IT'S AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff means cloth or fabric, and satin is a glossy woven fabric.

clue.text: Patient attention expected from 2. dn

parts.note: the care a sick person hopes for from the answer to 2 Down, the woman who tends people

explanation.surface: What a careful carer is expected to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 Down is NURSE; 'Patient' reads as 'tolerant' but means a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical care given to someone who is ill.
